header: The Indian rupee sign (₹, U+20B9) in the text of a circular (step 42b). It is printed before amounts all through the circulars, and OCR cannot read it: an OCR engine's English model can have no rupee glyph at all: on 342 degraded renders (19 Oct 2026, 19 font faces) one engine wrote the sign as 2, 7, 3, %, ¥, €, ®, =, ~, *, X, t, F or Z, or dropped it. When the sign touches the amount, a digit-like guess FUSES into the number: `₹15,000` became `215,000` and `715,000`, `₹112.50` became `2112.50`. That is a wrong amount that looks right; it caused the invented "275,000" of the gift-card circular. What the text alone can do (the glyph itself is a different job: it needs the page image): I find an amount with ONE EXTRA LEADING DIGIT (2, 3 or 7, the digits seen) when the SAME PAGE also states the same amount without that digit (`(215,000)` with `Rs 15,000` elsewhere), and I record it as UNCONFIRMED, so the answer card refuses an answer that rests on it (circularAnswer.ts, the confirmation gate). The text cannot know the truth: a page may state both `15,000` and `215,000` for real, which is rare (the shorter amount must have 4 or more digits, and stand at least as often as the longer). I report a symbol written before an amount where no symbol can belong (`% 15,000`, `¥ 1,50,000/-`) too: it is the rupee sign read as a symbol (and a picture of the printed sign). This file is pure; currency.selftest.ts unit-tests it.

symbols.name: RUPEE_MARK_WORDS
doc: What may stand in front of an amount to say it is in rupees, besides the sign: Rs, Rs., INR, Rupees, and Hindi रु / रू.

symbols.name: SLOT_DIGITS
doc: The digits that a printed rupee sign was seen to fuse into an amount as.

symbols.name: SLOT_SYMBOLS
doc: These symbols never belong in front of an amount in a circular (a percent sign comes AFTER its number), so when one stands there I treat it as the rupee sign misread.

symbols.name: canon
doc: I use the same canonical form as readingCheck.numbersOf: no thousands commas, and every separator of a date, time or reference written ".".

members.name: value
doc: The amount with the extra leading digit, in canonical form.

members.name: base
doc: The amount the page also states, without it.

symbols.name: attachedDigitSuspects
doc: Finds amounts that are an amount the page also states, with one more digit (2, 3 or 7) in front of it: probably the rupee sign read as a digit.

members.name: amount
doc: The amount after it, in canonical form.

symbols.name: rupeeSlotJunk
doc: Finds a symbol that cannot belong before an amount, standing right before one: I read it as the rupee sign misread as that symbol.

symbols.name: slotChecks
symbols.sig: export function slotChecks(pages: { page: number; text: string }[]): NewCheck[]
doc: The checks of the pages of one circular: I mark each amount with a stray leading digit UNCONFIRMED, and this check confirms nothing.

doc: The same from a circular's stored chunks (the input of checkRowsFor).

behaviours: the sign is U+20B9
the digits seen fused in front of an amount are 2, 3 and 7
REAL: the gift card (215,000 next to Rs 15,000)
REAL: 2112.50 next to 112.50 (the premium)
REAL: 715,000 and 315,000 (the digits 7 and 3 were seen too)
a leading 4, which was never seen for the sign, is not concluded about
Devanagari digits are read: (२१५,०००) next to रु. १५,०००
what a second reader wrote in [handwritten: ...] is not part of the page
an amount with no shorter twin on the page is left alone (nothing says it is wrong)
a short base is too common to conclude from (Rs 500 and 2500)
a reference number is not an amount with a stray digit (2026/50)
a number that ends with a year is not (931/2025 next to 2025)
a date is not (20-08-2026 next to 0-08-2026 cannot be)
the shorter amount must stand at least as often as the longer
two amounts that both stand, the longer once and the shorter twice: concluded about the longer
REAL: (% 15,000), the sign read as a percent sign
REAL: ¥ 1,50,000/-, € and ® before an amount
REAL: up to % 20,000 only
a percent sign AFTER its number is a percent sign (50% 15,000 employees; 5% of 15,000)
an equals sign is not reported (Total = 15,000 is legitimate)
a written mark is not reported (Rs. 15,000)
the second reader is told: the sign is a currency mark, never a digit; copy it as printed; never write it as 2, 3, 7, %, Z or T; keep the printed digits
...and its other rules are still there (the prompt was extended, not replaced)
the synthesis prompt says the sign is never a digit, names the stray-digit case and what to report
a page with a suspect gets a check: unconfirmed, nothing confirmed, the reader named; a clean page gets none
a number two pages agree on (215,000 on both) is confirmed, and the single-page suspicion is lifted
when no other page confirms it, the suspicion stands and both readers are named
combining again changes nothing
GATE: on a single-page circular, 215,000 is refused: the page itself also says Rs. 15,000
GATE: Rs. 15,000 from the same page passes
the checks of a circular from its chunks carry the fingerprint of the text that is stored
a one-chunk circular with no suspect gets no rows

REAL: on the ${pilot.length} hard pages of the pilot, in both readings, the ONLY amount flagged is the real misread of the gift-card Hindi page's old reading (215,000 where the circular says Rs 15,000): no false alarm anywhere else, and Gemini's reading of that page is not flagged
...and the hand-made truth of that page says the amount is 15,000
the GPAIS pair still gets only its twin confirmation from the twin check, and no suspect
